annotation.title_clean: Evaluating productivity and accountability in IoT-enabled robotic systems with citizenship-like responsibilities
annotation.title_en: Evaluating productivity and accountability in IoT-enabled robotic systems with citizenship-like responsibilities
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kanade, T.M.; Y, H.; Pulekar, D.; Savale, T.K.; Kamble, S.M.
annotation.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research and Scientific Studies
annotation.summary_en: Mixed-method journal article evaluating IoT-enabled industrial and logistics robots given citizenship-like responsibilities. Finds robots excel in consistency, scalability and energy efficiency, but more autonomy does not always improve performance, and accountability mechanisms have limited effect on efficiency. Calls for multidisciplinary ethical and accountability frameworks.
key_provisions_or_claims: IoT-enabled robots outperform humans in consistency, scalability and energy efficiency
Greater autonomy does not necessarily improve performance
Accountability mechanisms aid transparency but have limited impact on task efficiency
Citizenship-like responsibilities for robots challenge traditional frameworks of responsibility and agency
Calls for multidisciplinary ethical and accountability frameworks in design and deployment
